newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanians back govt despite reform pain - survey.
newsitem.headline: Romanians back govt despite reform pain - survey.

text.p: Most Romanians have kept faith with the government, despite tough reforms which have sent prices soaring and the prospect of continued austerity, an opinion poll showed on Friday.

The survey, by independent pollsters IRSOP, showed 53 percent of Romanians were confident in the ruling centrists, while 48 percent credited them with the ability to outperform their leftist predecessors, ousted at the polls last November.
A large majority, 62 percent, rated recent price rises as their chief concern. But more than a third of the 1,048 respondents said they saw prospects for an economic upturn within one year.

Monthly inflation slowed to 4.3 percent in May after hitting a record 30.7 percent in March, putting new pressure on Romanians. The average monthly wage is some $80, half as much as before the 1989 fall of communism.
Despite continued economic hardship, the Democratic Convention bloc, backbone of the ruling coalition, was credited with 50 percent support.
The survey showed reformist President Emil Constantinescu and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea led popularity ratings with 67 percent and 62 percent respectively.
